catalogue.description: Explicit plane realizations of the elliptically admissible extension orbits at the natural Halphen index. Each entry records a coefficient field, a smooth plane cubic, the complete ordered cluster of nine centers, and the classes of the prime (-2)-curves in the basis (L,E_1,...,E_9).
catalogue.theorem: For each of the twenty-six entries, blowing up the displayed ordered cluster gives an extremal Halphen surface of the stated index and extension orbit; the displayed class-matrix rows are the classes of unique geometrically integral (-2)-curves and form the declared affine ADE configuration.
catalogue.exclusion: The split D6+2A1 extension is absent because its middle group is (Z/2)^3, which cannot be a subgroup of a smooth elliptic curve; the two nonzero extension orbits are represented.

sections.label: Field and parameters
sections.tex:
Let \(i^2=-1\), \(u\) be transcendental, and put
\[
k=\mathbb Q(i)(u),\qquad
a=\frac{2u}{1+u^2},\qquad b=\frac{1-u^2}{1+u^2}.
\]

sections.label: Open locus
sections.tex:
Inside \(u(1-u^2)(1+u^2)\ne0\), remove the closed locus where
one of the ten unique root curves ceases to be geometrically integral.
The remaining open is nonempty, as certified by \(u=1/2\).

sections.label: Normal and extension
sections.tex:
With
\[
Q=(-a:ia(1+a):1),\qquad P=(1+b:-b(1+b):1),
\]
one has \(N=P-Q\), \(\operatorname{ord}(N)=4\),
the middle group is
\(\langle Q,P\rangle\simeq(\mathbb Z/4)^2\), and \(\xi=0\).

sections.label: Open locus
sections.tex:
Inside \(t(t-1)(2t-1)(8t^2-8t+1)\ne0\), remove the closed locus
where the points collide or one of the ten unique root curves ceases to be
geometrically integral.  The remaining open is nonempty, as certified by
\(t=2\).

sections.label: Normal and extension
sections.tex:
Here \(P=(0:0:1)\) has order eight and
\[
Q=\left(q:\frac{b-(1-c)q}{2}:1\right)
\]
is independent two-torsion. Thus
\(N=Q+2P\), \(\operatorname{ord}(N)=4\),
the middle group is
\(\langle Q,P\rangle\simeq\mathbb Z/2\oplus\mathbb Z/8\), and \(\xi=2\).

sections.label: Field and parameters
sections.tex:
Let \(\Gamma_{\rm cyc}\) be the normalization of
\(\Psi_{\rm cyc}(s,u)=0\), put
\[
k=\mathbb Q(\Gamma_{\rm cyc}),\qquad
w=\frac{s^2u-su-s+u}{s(u-1)},
\]

sections.label: Open locus
sections.tex: We take the complement in the indicated normalization of the zeros and poles of the written denominators and cubic discriminant, the pairwise-collision locus of the nine projective points, and the closed loci where the normal class loses its stated exact order or one of the unique root curves loses geometric integrality.

sections.label: Cubic
sections.tex:
With
\[
\begin{aligned}
A&=-sw+s-u+w,\\
B&=suw-su+u-w,\\
D&=-su^2w+su^2-su+2sw-s+u^2-uw,
\end{aligned}
\]
\[
\begin{aligned}
G=\mathscr G\!\bigl(&A,B,sw(u-1),D,\\
                    &uA,-su(u-1),suw(u-1)\bigr).
\end{aligned}
\]

sections.label: Normal and extension
sections.tex: The class $N=\mathcal O_G(3)-\sum_i p_i$ has exact order $4$. The middle group $\langle p_i-p_1\rangle$ is $\mathbb Z/16$; its quotient by $\langle N\rangle$ is $\mathbb Z/4$, and the extension class is the cyclic orbit $\xi=\pm1$.

sections.label: Open locus
sections.tex: We take the complement in the indicated normalization of the zeros and poles of the written denominators and cubic discriminant, the pairwise-collision locus of the nine projective points, and the closed loci where the normal class loses its stated exact order or one of the unique root curves loses geometric integrality.

sections.label: Normal and extension
sections.tex: The class $N=\mathcal O_G(3)-\sum_i p_i$ has exact order $4$. The middle group $\langle p_i-p_1\rangle$ is $(\mathbb Z/4)^2$; its quotient by $\langle N\rangle$ is $\mathbb Z/4$, and the extension is split ($\xi=0$).
